chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi, from Mus'ab ibn Yazeed, from al-'Awwam ibn al-Zubayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who softens his face softens his knowledge.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean when a person's face is described as 'soft' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarly tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores the inseparable link between akhlaq (ethics) and ilm (knowledge), positing that physical humility is a manifestation of intellectual receptivity. It reflects the concept that a 'soft face' indicates a heart free from arrogance, thereby allowing divine knowledge to settle deeply, a view supported by commentators who see it as a sign of spiritual maturity and approachability in the learned.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al Nahdy, from Mus’ab Bin Yazeed, from Al Awwan Bin al Zubeyr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who softens his face would soften his knowledge’.
en.sarwar: 3. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Nahdi from Mus’ab ibn Yazid from al -‘Awwam ibn al-Zubayr from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
One whose face is thin (bashful and shy) has thin knowledge.’”
